PR surface: Source +1, Tests -2. Total -1 across 3 files.

target.title: fix(agents): handle stdin stream errors in docker sandbox execution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Docker sandbox commands could crash or hang when the child stdin stream failed while writing command input.

## Why This Change Was Made

stdin now uses the existing first-error lifecycle shared by stdout and stderr: record the error, terminate the Docker child, and reject after close. Coverage is consolidated into the existing Docker process tests; PR-only proof scaffolding was removed.

## User Impact

Docker-backed sandbox file and shell commands fail promptly with the original stdin error instead of crashing the agent runtime or leaving a command pending.

## Evidence

- Clean head `b30ad2da0cd817742be2998ddbb7ab7fc4125042` is a three-file delta on current main: runtime, focused regression coverage, and one sibling test-double contract repair.
- Sanitized public-network AWS Crabbox `cbx_fa246128d768`, exact runtime/test blob identity with reviewed head `710ad0b7acf2f1310181e7b10c821e1df11f1d7b`:
  - run `run_718076c920a0`: `pnpm test src/agents/sandbox/docker.test.ts` — 6/6 passed.
  - run `run_00abac53cbf2`: real long-lived Node child, injected stdin failure rejected in 58 ms and terminated the child.
- Final head keeps the live-proven production blob `1ffc3f7f8e0029e57fceceb49971547f5c5c606e`; later changes only repaired test-double typing.
- Broad CI exposed older test-double typing gaps: sibling stdin lacked Node's EventEmitter contract, and a dynamic stream lookup needed narrowing before `emit`. Both mocks now model the real stream contract instead of adding a production fallback.
- Fresh Codex AutoReview: clean, confidence 0.90.
